text:
carmen: Quick heads-up — saw repeated tail latency spikes (~200-400ms) for a handful of tenants on eu-west-rack18 this morning. Looks correlated with a pack of long-context generation jobs on a dedicated slice.

lee: ugh. any gpu mem pressure or NVLink errors in the node logs?

carmen: mem looks steady. nvlink warnings around 09:12 for three pods, repeated soft preempts. attaching scrubbed logs: 
```
[2026-03-12T09:12:03Z] pod/tenant-A-gen: GPU0 soft-preempt: stall 320ms
[2026-03-12T09:12:05Z] pod/tenant-B-rerank: NVLINK ecc-corrected: minor
[2026-03-12T09:12:06Z] allocator: slab-frag ratio=0.78, warm-pool-writes=high
```

anya: is this multi-tenant on the same dedicated pool? thought dedicated slices were isolated.

carmen: They’re on a fractional carveout we call "dedicated-slab-6" — it's shared across 4 tenants (reserved weights). Seems like heavy long-seq jobs from tenant-A caused KV cache churn and IO jitter that spilled into others.

tom: if it's KV cache churn + long context, we could try throttling preemptions and bumping the kvcache retention for that slice. But that will increase GPU memory per-slice and cost.

lee: i've seen similar with vGPU slices — scheduler pack density matters. Maybe the allocator put mixed workloads (latency-sensitive + batchy long-context) on same host. Can we tag latency-sensitive routes and prefer hard isolation?

anya: Product will push back on hard isolation because customers expect lower costs. Any quick mitigations we can run?

carmen: short term: 1) soft throttle tenant-A long-context jobs (rate-limit at proxy) 2) pin tenant-A to a temporary warm pool with isolated KV cache 3) run a probe to detect kvcache spill -> auto-shield tenant when threshold hit.

tom: i can sketch a canary. Plan: change routing rule for tenant-A in eu-west to prefer warmpool-iso-1 for next 2h, fallback to default. Add an SLI alert for kvcache-regen > 10/s.

sre-bot: deploy started: routing-change for tenant-A -> warmpool-iso-1 (canary) by tom at 2026-03-12T10:02:00Z :gear:

lee: can we also add an allocation weight floor so the allocator doesn't co-locate batchy jobs with low-latency tenants on the same GPU? something like avoid co-locating if expected p95>150ms.

anya: rough cost calc? if we carve out a hard-isolated slice (one whole GPU) for tenant-A, what's the monthly burn delta?

tom: quick numbers: gpu-hour cost (infra) 3.2 USD, tenant-A load avg 0.2 GPU -> currently shared-cost ~0.64 USD/hr. Hard isolate 1 GPU = 3.2 USD/hr, delta ~+2.56 USD/hr -> ~+1840 USD/month (24/7). If we only isolate during spikes via warmpool prefill, effective cost much lower.

carmen: agreed. let's avoid full-time isolate. We'll do conditional warmpool fallback + throttling and measure. If p95 for other tenants still >120ms after 6h, escalate to (a) temporary whole-GPU isolate for offending tenant during business hours, (b) longer term: revise fractional carveout sizing.

lee: note: allocator change might require a short rolling restart of packer to pick up new anti-colocate rule. schedule late-night.

tom: i'll run canary now and post results in ~30m. @anya can you draft the cost note and customer impact phrasing if we need to temporarily throttle?

anya: on it. will include exact numbers + suggested customer message template.

sre-bot: canary finished: 600/600 requests routed to warmpool-iso-1, observed tenant-A p99 drop from 560ms -> 220ms, other tenants p99 stable. metrics: https://telemetry/redwood/eu-west/rack18/canary/1715562345

carmen: nice. initial win. can we enable auto-shield logic: if KV_REGEN_RATE > 12 and GPU_SOFT_PREEMPTS > 3 in 5m -> route new requests to warmpool-iso-1?

tom: yea i can add a short rule in the router. needs change in config repo: 
```
- condition: kvcache_regen_rate > 12 and soft_preempts >=3
  action: route -> warmpool-iso-1
  ttl: 10m
```
apply as canary in eu-west only.

lee: please also add telemetry tag 'isolation_trigger=v1' so we can track cost delta.

anya: i pushed the customer note draft to product-review. dm-ing legal for language around "temporary throttling".

carmen: tl;dr: don't do permanent carveouts unless SLA demands. use adaptive warmpool shielding + router triggers for now. We'll reconvene if rate of these incidents > 1/week.

tom: follow-ups: i'll open a task with steps (add router rule, add telemetry tag, schedule allocator restart for anti-colocate rule) and link the canary graphs.

lee: and long-term: we should evaluate a cost model that charges partially-isolated tenants a small premium for stability. helps align incentives.

anya: noted. product will consider.

sre-bot: ticket created: INFRA-9241 "canary: adaptive-warmpool-shielding eu-west-rack18" by tom

carmen: thanks team. will mark this thread resolved unless we see repeat later today. :white_check_mark:
